reviewers.summary: The page-read counter now verifies the 201-page case extracts zero pages. The stream limit remains bypassable because filter detection does not account for valid escaped PDF names.

findingList.message: The decoded-stream limit can be bypassed with a PDF name escape: normalize PDF names before checking filters or reject escaped filter names.

evidence.codePathTraced: CheckStreamLimits detects a filter only when the raw header contains the literal `/Filter`. PDF names can encode characters with `#xx`, so PdfPig recognizes `/#46ilter` as `/Filter` while this check treats the stream as unfiltered and only counts its compressed length.
evidence.failureScenario: A presenter submits a PDF under 10 MB with a short Flate stream whose dictionary uses `/#46ilter /FlateDecode` and whose decoded content is very large. The precheck accepts it under the 8 MiB cap, then PdfPig decompresses it in the API process and can exhaust service memory. This leaves the decompression resource-exhaustion risk from the prior round reachable (OWASP A06:2025, Insecure Design).

reviewers.summary: The revised test observes zero page-text reads for a 201-page PDF. However, PDF name escaping bypasses the new decompression check, so an under-limit compressed document can still exhaust API resources.

findingList.message: The stream limit check can be bypassed with a PDF-escaped filter name, leaving decompression unbounded during in-process extraction (OWASP A06:2025).

evidence.codePathTraced: CheckStreamLimits detects filters with a literal "/Filter" substring. PDF names may encode characters with #xx escapes, which PdfPig decodes when it reads the document.
evidence.failureScenario: A PDF under the byte limit uses `/F#69lter /FlateDecode` and a short compressed stream that expands beyond the decoded-byte cap. This check treats the stream as unfiltered and counts only its compressed length; PdfPig then decompresses it during page text extraction, potentially exhausting API process resources.

reviewers.summary: The decoded-stream cap addresses the earlier Flate expansion path, but extracted text is only checked after PdfPig materializes it. A crafted font mapping can still cause excessive API memory use.

findingList.message: OWASP A06:2025 (Insecure Design): the decoded-stream cap does not bound the text PdfPig materializes. Enforce an extraction bound before the full page text is allocated.

evidence.codePathTraced: The stream check caps decoded stream bytes, but page.Text is materialized before its length is checked at line 126. A font’s ToUnicode mapping can expand each glyph into a longer string than its encoded content.
evidence.failureScenario: A presenter submits a PDF under the 10 MB input limit whose streams total under 8 MiB, but whose font mapping expands repeated glyphs into a very large amount of text. PdfPig allocates that text in the API process at page.Text before the limit check, potentially exhausting service memory.
